items.t: "Burnaby Hospital" is the GVR board sub-area name used in the SnapStats GVR report for Burnaby — it is named for the hospital, not for a City neighbourhood plan. The sub-area is the residential area around Burnaby Hospital in central Burnaby, south of Canada Way and west of Deer Lake, with the hospital campus at 3935 Kincaid St. The City publishes no street-by-street written boundary for the MLS sub-area; exact MLS boundary streets are not verified. Nearby areas: Sperling-Duthie and Deer Lake to the east, Burnaby Lake to the north-east across Canada Way, Cascade Heights to the south, Forest Glen and Metrotown to the west and south-west.

Where the condo stock concentrates: it barely does. Burnaby's tower and low-rise condo stock concentrates in its town centres (Metrotown to the south-west is this area's main shopping and condo centre), not around the hospital.

Main streets: Canada Way is the main east–west road at the area's north edge, Kincaid Street serves the hospital campus, and Deer Lake Parkway and Sperling Avenue link east to Deer Lake and City Hall (4949 Canada Way).

Transit: there is no SkyTrain station inside the sub-area; buses operate on Kincaid Street at the campus, and the nearest Millennium Line station is Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station at Sperling Avenue and Lougheed Highway, north-east across the Deer Lake / Burnaby Lake side (station walking distance for a specific address: Not verified).

blocks.text: Good to know about Burnaby Hospital

items.t: The sub-area is a hospital with houses around it, not a condo district.

The hospital plan was renewed on a specific date. On September 21, 2026 the Province announced $210 million for the emergency department and surgical unit to proceed immediately, with expanded cancer care and a new acute-care tower to follow, building on the March 2026 opening of the new six-storey pavilion — construction on Kincaid Street is a multi-year condition of living beside the campus, not a one-season project.

The one strata complex carries two build years. The building directory dates 3980 Canada Way to 1984; a unit listing in the same complex says 1986. Neither source is a strata-plan record — a buyer ordering documents should expect the strata plan registration, not either published year, to govern.

Deer Lake's boardwalk is mid-replacement. The section of Deer Lake boardwalk by the boat launch, immediately east of the sub-area, closed September 21, 2026 for a full replacement, with completion scheduled by winter 2027 and a signed detour via Sperling Avenue and Deer Lake Drive.

The governing plans are both new. The Burnaby 2050 OCP was adopted December 9, 2025 and takes precedence over older community-plan maps, the Cascade Heights Community Plan at the sub-area's south side was adopted in March 2025, and Zoning Bylaw 2026 took effect July 1, 2026 — listing copy or advice citing the 1998 OCP or the old zoning bylaw is two documents out of date.

City Hall is the east-edge neighbour. Burnaby City Hall sits at 4949 Canada Way just east of the sub-area at Deer Lake, and Deer Lake Park (6450 Deer Lake Ave) — with the Burnaby Art Gallery, Shadbolt Centre for the Arts, Burnaby Village Museum and Hart House — is the cultural centre the townhouse stock markets itself against.

Main streets and transit: Canada Way is the main east-west road at the area's north edge, Kincaid Street serves the hospital campus, and Deer Lake Parkway and Sperling Avenue link east to Deer Lake and City Hall (4949 Canada Way). There is no SkyTrain station inside the sub-area; buses operate on Kincaid Street at the campus, and the nearest Millennium Line station is Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station at Sperling Avenue and Lougheed Highway, north-east across the Deer Lake / Burnaby Lake side (station walking distance for a specific address: Not verified).

Schools: SD41 (Burnaby) schools in or beside the sub-area include Douglas Road Elementary (K–7), 4861 Canada Way, Cascade Heights Elementary (K–7), 4343 Smith Ave at the south side, and Burnaby Central Secondary (8–12), 6011 Deer Lake Parkway at the east side.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Burnaby Hospital

items.t: Form B diligence (the 1 strata complex above): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. For a 1980s wood-frame townhouse strata, the depreciation report and Form B are the central diligence documents — envelope, roof and plumbing cycles sit in them, not in listing copy.
